clinical_category: Advanced liver disease - multidisciplinary care coordination
blueprint_topic: Handoff, referrals, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continuity of care
stem: A client with advanced liver disease is preparing for discharge. The hepatology, nutrition, and social-work plans contain different follow-up instructions, and the client is unsure which appointments and referrals are required. Which action by the nurse best supports continuity of care?

options.A: Reconcile the plan with the multidisciplinary team, clarify unresolved orders or referrals, update the care plan and discharge information, and ensure an accurate handoff so the client knows the next steps.
options.B: Give the client each discipline's separate instructions without clarification because coordination between services is outside the nurse's role.
options.C: Cancel specialty follow-up and direct the client to use only one provider so conflicting recommendations cannot occur.
options.D: Limit care coordination to insurance authorization and leave clinical referrals, handoff, and plan-of-care discrepancies unresolved.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places multidisciplinary collaboration, handoff, referral assessment, implementation of provider orders, updating the plan of care, advocacy, and use of resources to promote quality care within Management of Care. AASLD also describes advanced/decompensated cirrhosis as a condition with multidisciplinary physical, psychosocial, nutritional, and palliative-care needs, reinforcing the importance of coordinated care across services. B is incorrect because the nurse has an explicit Management-of-Care role in collaboration and continuity and should not knowingly pass unresolved discrepancies to the client. C is incorrect because eliminating indicated specialty services is not an appropriate method of resolving conflicting instructions. D is too narrow: administrative authorization may be one component of coordination, but it does not replace clinical reconciliation, referrals, handoff, or care-plan management. The final item tests an observable nursing coordination decision rather than memorization of a generic case-manager job description.
educational_objective: Coordinate complex discharge care by reconciling multidisciplinary recommendations, clarifying orders and referrals, updating the plan of care, and providing an accurate handoff so the client has a coherent follow-up plan.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN); American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)
source_document_title: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; Palliative Care and Symptom-Based Management in Decompensated Cirrhosis
source_version_date: NCSBN Test Plan effective April 2026; AASLD Practice Guidance updated April 2022 and current on the AASLD practice-guideline site in 2026
source_locator: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan → Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care, printed p. 7 (PDF pageno 10): provide/receive handoff; identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members; receive, verify and implement provider orders; assess need for referrals and obtain necessary orders; initiate/evaluate/update client plan of care; recognize limitations and utilize resources; utilize resources to promote quality client care. AASLD 'Palliative Care and Symptom-Based Management in Decompensated Cirrhosis' → Practice Guidance overview: decompensated cirrhosis carries complex physical, psychosocial and caregiver needs and palliative care is multidisciplinary specialized care.
source_claim_supported: The current NCSBN test plan directly supports multidisciplinary collaboration, handoff, referral coordination, provider-order verification, care-plan updating and resource use as Management-of-Care nursing activities; current AASLD guidance independently supports the multidisciplinary nature of advanced cirrhosis care.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care, printed p. 7 (PDF pageno 10): provide/receive handoff, collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, assess referral needs, implement provider orders, initiate/evaluate/update the plan of care and utilize resources to promote quality care.
correction_summary: Total quality rebuild. The source item asked for a generic definition of case management and cited a generic CMSA homepage. The final version tests a concrete NCLEX Management-of-Care decision involving conflicting multidisciplinary discharge instructions, referral/order clarification, care-plan reconciliation and handoff. The generic source was replaced by the official 2026 NCSBN Test Plan, with AASLD used only to support the multidisciplinary context of advanced liver disease.
audit_findings: The source concept was directionally reasonable but too generic and used a homepage-level case-management citation that did not meet the exact-locator standard.

Fresh review of the official 2026 NCSBN Test Plan directly supports handoff, multidisciplinary collaboration, referrals, provider-order verification, plan-of-care updating and resource use under Management of Care.
AASLD independently confirms that advanced/decompensated cirrhosis involves multidisciplinary care needs, supporting the clinical context without creating a disease-specific coordination rule.
Distractors test siloed care, inappropriate elimination of specialty follow-up and administrative-only coordination; none is defensible.

Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct coordination action with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported scope expansion, locator defect, blueprint mismatch, or unresolved conflict.
